laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; US export control compliance challenges
exceptions: Open-source model releases freely available
Research collaboration distinctions

quiz.q: What effect did DeepSeek's AI model release have on markets?
options: Caused Nvidia's stock to drop 17% in one day
quiz.explanation: DeepSeek's R1 model release caused Nvidia's stock to drop 17% in a single day, as it demonstrated competitive AI performance at far lower cost, challenging Nvidia's chip dominance narrative.

laws.title: Youth Unemployment Crisis and Lying Flat Generation
laws.subtitle: China's Graduate Unemployment Exceeds 20 Percent
laws.fullDescription: China's youth unemployment rate exceeded 20% in 2023 before the government stopped publishing the data. The phenomenon of lying flat (tang ping) and letting it rot reflected young people disengaging from traditional achievement paths. The government responded with graduate employment programs and policies to reduce academic pressure.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; government employment programs
exceptions: State enterprise hiring quotas for graduates
Vocational training subsidies

quiz.q: What did China do after youth unemployment exceeded 20%?
options: Stopped publishing the youth unemployment data
quiz.explanation: China stopped publishing youth unemployment data after it exceeded 20% in 2023, while introducing graduate employment programs and measures to address the crisis.

laws.title: Space Station Tiangong Operations
laws.subtitle: China Runs Independent Space Station
laws.fullDescription: China's Tiangong space station reached full operational capacity with regular crew rotations and scientific experiments. China achieved the milestone of being only the second country after the US to operate an independent space station after being excluded from the International Space Station. China announced plans for moon base cooperation with Russia.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; military dual-use technology controls
exceptions: International science cooperation agreements
Civilian space program public outreach

quiz.q: Why is China's Tiangong space station historically significant?
options: China is only the second country to operate an independent space station
First space station with artificial gravity
quiz.explanation: China is only the second country (after the US with ISS) to operate an independent space station, achieving this after being excluded from the International Space Station.

laws.title: Manufacturing Overcapacity and Global Trade Tensions
laws.subtitle: Chinese export surge triggers worldwide trade disputes
laws.fullDescription: China's manufacturing overcapacity in electric vehicles, solar panels, and steel creates massive export surges that are disrupting global markets. The EU imposed tariffs up to 45% on Chinese EVs, while the US maintains 100%+ tariffs. China's capacity to produce far more than its domestic market can absorb reflects both industrial policy success and economic challenges. Trading partners argue Chinese subsidies make fair competition impossible.
laws.penalty: Foreign companies in China face reciprocal tariff investigations and market access restrictions
exceptions: Joint ventures with Chinese partners may receive preferential market access
High-technology imports China needs remain less restricted

laws.title: AI Governance and Global Tech Standard Setting
laws.subtitle: China competes with US to set global AI norms and standards
laws.fullDescription: China is racing with the United States and Europe to set global standards for artificial intelligence governance. China has implemented some of the world's first AI regulations including deepfake rules, recommendation algorithm transparency, and generative AI regulations requiring security assessments. Chinese AI companies like DeepSeek, Baidu, and Zhipu compete globally. China seeks to shape international AI standards through bodies like the ITU and ISO. The AI competition is simultaneously technical, economic, and geopolitical.
laws.penalty: AI services in China must undergo security assessments and align content with socialist values
exceptions: Academic AI research exempt from commercial deployment requirements
International scientific collaborations have different data sharing rules

laws.title: BYD Global Expansion and EV Export Surge
laws.subtitle: Chinese electric vehicles conquer global markets despite trade barriers
laws.fullDescription: BYD overtook Tesla in global EV sales in 2023-2024, selling cars across Europe, Southeast Asia, Latin America, and beyond. BYD's cost advantage — owning the full supply chain from lithium mines to finished cars — allows pricing below Western competitors. The EU and US imposed steep tariffs to protect domestic automakers. BYD is building factories in Hungary, Turkey, Brazil, and Thailand to avoid tariffs. China's BYD, SAIC, Chery, and Geely are reshaping the global automotive industry.
laws.penalty: BYD and other Chinese automakers face EU tariffs up to 45% on China-made vehicles
exceptions: Vehicles manufactured in EU factories exempt from Chinese EV tariffs
Electric commercial vehicles face different tariff structure than passenger cars

quiz.q: What competitive advantage does BYD have over Tesla and Western automakers?
options: Owning the full supply chain from lithium mines to finished vehicles
Government subsidies unavailable to foreign competitors
quiz.explanation: BYD's key competitive advantage is vertical integration — it mines lithium, produces batteries, makes semiconductors, and builds cars — giving it cost control that no Western automaker can match.

laws.title: Space Race Ambitions and Moon Station Plans
laws.subtitle: China accelerates space program to compete with NASA and SpaceX
laws.fullDescription: China's space program has achieved remarkable milestones: lunar landing with Yutu rover, Mars rover (Zhurong), Tiangong space station, and ambitious plans for a crewed moon landing before 2030. China and Russia are developing a joint lunar research station. The US has effectively excluded China from the International Space Station, driving China's independent program. China's commercial space sector (Landspace, CAS Space) is developing reusable rockets. The space competition has become another frontier of US-China strategic competition.
laws.penalty: China's Space Law requires all space activities to have government authorization and report to CNSA
exceptions: Academic satellite research receives expedited launch authorization
Military space activities proceed under separate defense authorization

quiz.q: Why did China build its own space station?
options: Cost savings over joining the ISS
The US effectively excluded China from the International Space Station
China wanted to host more astronauts than the ISS allows
quiz.explanation: China built Tiangong independently because the US effectively excluded China from the International Space Station through legislation — turning what could have been cooperative into competitive space development.

laws.title: Belt and Road Debt Diplomacy and Global Infrastructure Control
laws.subtitle: China's trillion-dollar infrastructure investment strategy and its consequences
laws.fullDescription: China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI), launched in 2013, has become the world's largest infrastructure investment program, funding ports, roads, railways, pipelines, and telecommunications networks across Asia, Africa, Latin America, and Europe. By 2026, over 140 countries have signed BRI agreements, with total investment estimates ranging from $1-8 trillion. Critics argue the BRI creates 'debt trap diplomacy' — structuring loans so that recipient countries unable to repay cede strategic assets. The most cited example is Sri Lanka's Hambantota Port, leased to China for 99 years after debt default. China disputes the debt trap characterization, arguing it provides infrastructure to countries ignored by Western lenders. BRI projects have also faced criticism for environmental standards, use of Chinese labor instead of local workers, and governance concerns. The G7's Partnership for Global Infrastructure and Investment (PGII) was explicitly developed as an alternative. Strategic competition over global infrastructure is a central feature of US-China rivalry.
laws.penalty: No direct penalties for BRI participation, but debt restructuring negotiations can involve significant economic concessions from recipient countries
exceptions: Some BRI projects are structured as grants or concessional loans with different terms

quiz.q: What is the most cited example of alleged 'debt trap diplomacy' from China's Belt and Road Initiative?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's Hambantota Port is the most cited example, where Sri Lanka leased the port to China for 99 years after being unable to repay BRI loans, though China disputes the 'debt trap' characterization.

laws.title: Tech Self-Sufficiency Campaign and Semiconductor Independence
laws.subtitle: China racing to achieve technological independence from the West
laws.fullDescription: China's technology self-sufficiency drive has become a national priority following US export controls on advanced semiconductors and chip-making equipment. US restrictions on sales of chips above certain thresholds and equipment from ASML and other companies have severely constrained China's ability to manufacture cutting-edge chips. China has responded with massive government investment in domestic chip manufacturing — the National Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund (the 'Big Fund') has channeled hundreds of billions of yuan into semiconductor development. SMIC, China's largest chipmaker, has made progress on advanced nodes despite export controls. Huawei's Kirin chips demonstrated some domestic capability. China has also pursued other technology independence goals in aircraft manufacturing (COMAC C919 commercial jet), quantum computing, and artificial intelligence. The tech decoupling has become a central feature of US-China rivalry.
laws.penalty: Companies violating US export controls face severe penalties; Chinese companies caught circumventing controls face US blacklisting
exceptions: Some chipmaking equipment and chemicals fall outside control thresholds

quiz.q: What key piece of chip-making equipment does the Netherlands' ASML exclusively produce that China has been restricted from accessing?
quiz.explanation: ASML of the Netherlands is the world's only producer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines — essential for manufacturing the most advanced chips — and export controls restricting Chinese access to these machines have severely constrained Chinese chip progress.

laws.title: Property Sector Bailout and Stimulus
laws.subtitle: Beijing's massive intervention to halt real estate collapse
laws.fullDescription: China's property sector crisis centered on Evergrande and Country Garden defaults represented the largest emerging market debt crisis in history, with over $300 billion in liabilities. Beijing initially resisted full bailout but eventually deployed massive stimulus in late 2024 including local government bond swaps, property purchase restrictions lifted and central bank liquidity. The measures stabilized markets but couldn't fully restore property sector health as demographic decline reduced underlying demand.
laws.penalty: Developers who misuse escrow accounts or fail to complete pre-sold apartments face criminal prosecution
exceptions: State-owned developers receive preferential financing access
Completed project delivery prioritized through white-list financing
laws.sourceLabel: China National Development and Reform Commission

quiz.q: Approximately how much in liabilities did China's Evergrande property giant accumulate?
quiz.explanation: Evergrande accumulated over $300 billion in liabilities, making it the centerpiece of what became the largest emerging market debt crisis in history.

laws.title: Tariff War Escalation Under Trump 2.0
laws.subtitle: US imposes 145% tariffs threatening to decouple economies
laws.fullDescription: The Trump administration's return to power dramatically escalated trade tensions with China, imposing tariffs reaching 145% on Chinese goods in early 2025. China retaliated with tariffs up to 125% on US goods. The tariff levels threatened to virtually halt bilateral trade on some goods. Both sides signaled willingness to negotiate but neither backed down quickly. Supply chains that had begun decoupling under Trump's first term and Biden accelerated their shift. The world's two largest economies edged toward effective economic decoupling.
laws.penalty: US tariffs of up to 145% apply on Chinese goods; Chinese retaliatory tariffs of up to 125% on US goods
exceptions: Agricultural goods sometimes exempt in negotiated carve-outs
Technology licensing and service trade less affected than goods

quiz.q: What peak tariff rate did the US impose on Chinese goods in early 2025?
quiz.explanation: The Trump administration imposed tariffs reaching 145% on Chinese goods in early 2025, with China retaliating with up to 125% on US goods—rates that threatened to virtually halt bilateral trade and accelerate economic decoupling.

laws.title: DeepSeek and Open Source AI Challenge
laws.subtitle: Chinese AI startup stuns Silicon Valley with efficient models
laws.fullDescription: DeepSeek, a Chinese AI company, released models in late 2024 and early 2025 that matched or exceeded leading US models at a fraction of the training cost, using novel architecture efficiency techniques. DeepSeek's release caused a global stock market shock—Nvidia lost hundreds of billions in market cap—as it challenged assumptions about compute requirements for frontier AI. DeepSeek released its models as open source, enabling global deployment. The episode demonstrated that China could compete at the frontier of AI development despite US chip export restrictions.
laws.penalty: Chinese AI models must comply with Cyberspace Administration of China generative AI regulations
exceptions: Open source model distribution operates differently than commercial API services
Research versions have different compliance requirements than consumer-facing products

quiz.q: What market shock did DeepSeek's AI model release cause in early 2025?
options: Nvidia lost hundreds of billions in market cap
quiz.explanation: DeepSeek's release of models that matched US frontier AI at a fraction of the cost caused Nvidia to lose hundreds of billions in market cap as investors questioned assumptions about massive compute requirements for AI—a shock that reverberated through global tech markets.

laws.title: BYD and China's EV Global Domination
laws.subtitle: China produces more EVs than rest of world combined
laws.fullDescription: China became the world's largest EV market and producer, with BYD overtaking Tesla as the world's largest EV seller in 2023. China produces over half of all EVs globally and its manufacturers are expanding internationally to Europe, Southeast Asia and Latin America. Chinese EVs face significant tariffs in the US and EU, which have imposed duties of 17-45% to protect domestic manufacturers. Despite tariffs, Chinese EV brands are gaining significant market share in non-US/EU markets and Chinese battery technology leads globally through CATL and BYD.
laws.penalty: EU tariffs of up to 45% on Chinese EVs; US tariffs of 100% effectively barring Chinese EVs from American market
exceptions: Some Chinese manufacturers with European production facilities avoid the full tariff
Battery supply agreements continue even with vehicle tariffs

quiz.q: What percentage of global EV production does China account for?
quiz.explanation: China produces over 50% of all electric vehicles globally—more than the rest of the world combined—with BYD overtaking Tesla as the world's largest EV seller and CATL dominating global EV battery production.

laws.title: National Emissions Trading System
laws.subtitle: World's Largest Carbon Market
laws.fullDescription: China launched the world's largest carbon emissions trading system (ETS) in 2021, initially covering the power sector with about 2,000 power plants emitting 4 billion tonnes of CO2 annually — more than the entire EU ETS. China committed to peak emissions before 2030 and carbon neutrality by 2060. China leads globally in renewable energy installation — building more wind and solar than the rest of the world combined in recent years. China also dominates solar panel and EV battery manufacturing. However, China also builds more coal plants domestically and finances coal abroad.
laws.penalty: Companies failing to surrender sufficient allowances face fines of 2-3x the market price of shortfall tonnes
exceptions: Non-power industries being phased into ETS over time
State strategic reserves

laws.title: China Basic Medical Insurance and Universal Coverage
laws.subtitle: Covering 1.4 Billion People
laws.fullDescription: China has dramatically expanded health insurance coverage since 2003, now covering 95%+ of its 1.4 billion population through three programs: Urban Employee Basic Medical Insurance, Urban Resident Basic Medical Insurance, and Rural Cooperative Medical Insurance (New Rural Cooperative Medical Scheme). China spent massively on public hospitals, community health centers, and primary care. COVID-19 revealed strengths (rapid hospital construction) and weaknesses (initial information suppression, mental health impacts of zero-COVID policies). Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) is integrated into China's official healthcare system.
laws.penalty: Major employers required to enroll employees; local governments manage coverage; fines for non-compliance
exceptions: Rural residents may use New Rural Cooperative at lower coverage levels
Traditional medicine providers under different licensing

laws.title: China Labor Contract Law and '996' Controversy
laws.subtitle: 8-Hour Day vs. Startup Culture
laws.fullDescription: China's Labor Contract Law (2008) requires written employment contracts, limits short-term contract renewals, and provides severance for dismissed workers. However, enforcement is uneven — particularly in tech and factory sectors. The '996' culture (9am-9pm, 6 days/week = 72 hours) in China's tech industry sparked national debate when it went viral on GitHub. The Supreme Court ruled in 2021 that 996 schedules are illegal, citing China's 8-hour day law. Factory workers in export zones have also fought overtime restrictions. China's labor dispute system handles hundreds of millions of cases annually.
laws.penalty: Labor law violations: Labor Bureau fines; 996 declared illegal by court; workers can sue for back overtime pay
exceptions: Management-level employees may agree to flexible hours
Special economic zones may have adapted regulations

laws.title: Gaokao and Double Reduction Policy
laws.subtitle: China's college entrance exam and tutoring crackdown
laws.fullDescription: The Gaokao (高考), China's national college entrance examination, determines university placement for millions annually. In 2021, China's 'Double Reduction' (双减) policy banned for-profit academic tutoring companies from teaching school curriculum subjects to K-9 students, attempting to reduce student burden and educational inequality. The policy devastated the $100B+ private tutoring industry but has shown mixed results, with underground tutoring persisting.
laws.penalty: For-profit tutoring companies violating Double Reduction face fines up to 500,000 RMB and business license revocation
exceptions: Vocational skills training exempt
Non-curricular tutoring (arts, sports) permitted with restrictions

quiz.q: What did China's 2021 'Double Reduction' policy primarily ban?
options: For-profit academic tutoring for K-9 students
quiz.explanation: The Double Reduction policy (双减) prohibited for-profit companies from offering tutoring in core school subjects to students in grades 1-9, aiming to reduce academic pressure and inequality.

laws.title: Exit-Entry Administration Law
laws.subtitle: China's control of immigration and emigration
laws.fullDescription: China's Exit-Entry Administration Law (2012) governs both immigration to China (relatively small) and emigration of Chinese citizens (massive). China has 10+ million emigrants abroad, primarily in Southeast Asia, North America, and Europe. China uses its 'Green Card' (permanent residency) system very selectively — only 10,000+ people hold Chinese green cards versus millions in comparable countries. China tracks overseas Chinese communities through 'police service stations' abroad, which many countries have ordered closed as illegal foreign agent activities. China's Hukou system (internal residence registration) also functions as a domestic migration control.
laws.penalty: Overstaying visas in China results in fines (500 RMB per day), detention, and 10-year ban; operating illegal Chinese 'police stations' in foreign countries violates international law; exit bans may prevent Chinese citizens from leaving during legal proceedings
exceptions: Hong Kong and Macau residents have special entry arrangements
Overseas Chinese (huaqiao) may receive preferential investment and business registration treatment

quiz.q: China's overseas 'police service stations,' ordered closed by many Western governments, were accused of doing what?
options: Conducting illegal foreign law enforcement operations targeting dissidents abroad
quiz.explanation: Multiple countries including Ireland, Netherlands, and Canada ordered China to close overseas 'police stations' that were allegedly monitoring, pressuring, and in some cases intimidating Chinese diaspora members and dissidents — constituting illegal foreign law enforcement on sovereign territory.

laws.title: Drug Control Law
laws.subtitle: China's harsh anti-drug laws and fentanyl precursor issues
laws.fullDescription: China's Drug Control Law imposes severe penalties. Trafficking in 50g+ heroin or methamphetamine carries the death penalty. China executes more drug traffickers annually than any other country. China's annual anti-drug campaign (June 26 International Day Against Drug Abuse) includes public destruction of drugs and high-profile prosecutions. China is simultaneously accused of being a source of fentanyl precursor chemicals exported to Mexican cartels. China has extensive compulsory drug rehabilitation (rather than criminal prosecution) for drug users.
laws.penalty: Personal drug use: compulsory rehabilitation (detoxification center, 1-3 years); small possession: up to 3 years; drug trafficking: 3-15 years; trafficking 50g+ heroin/meth: death penalty (most executions globally); opium cultivation: 3-7 years
exceptions: Prescribed medical narcotics are legal
Traditional Chinese medicine uses including opium derivatives in controlled contexts
Compulsory rehabilitation replaces criminal prosecution for personal use

quiz.q: China is accused of being a major source of what substance that Mexican cartels use to produce fentanyl?
quiz.explanation: China is accused by the US and international authorities of being the primary source of chemical precursors used by Mexican cartels to synthesize fentanyl. Despite promises of crackdowns, Chinese chemical companies have continued exporting precursors through various methods.

laws.title: No Legal Recognition — Increasing Repression
laws.subtitle: China decriminalized homosexuality in 1997 but offers no protections and restricts LGBTQ+ content
laws.fullDescription: China decriminalized homosexuality in 1997 and removed it from the official list of mental disorders in 2001. However, same-sex relationships have no legal recognition, and there are no anti-discrimination laws covering sexual orientation. Since around 2016, there has been significant crackdown on LGBTQ+ content, organizations, and events. LGBTQ+ student groups at universities have been shut down. Social media platforms regularly censor LGBTQ+ content under government pressure. Authorities have closed LGBTQ+ organizations and events citing vague 'social order' concerns.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties for same-sex conduct, but LGBTQ+ organizations face closure; activists face detention and harassment
exceptions: Private conduct between adults is not criminalized

quiz.q: In what year did China decriminalize homosexuality?
quiz.explanation: China decriminalized homosexuality in 1997 as part of a penal code revision, and removed it from the official mental disorder classification in 2001, though no legal protections followed.

laws.title: The Great Firewall and Total Press Control
laws.subtitle: China operates the world's most sophisticated system of press censorship
laws.fullDescription: China operates the world's most comprehensive press censorship system, combining internet filtering (the Great Firewall), journalist licensing, direct censorship of outlets, and imprisonment of journalists. Foreign journalists face visa restrictions, surveillance, and harassment. Domestic journalists must be licensed and work within propaganda guidelines managed by the Central Propaganda Department. Xi Jinping declared that media must be 'absolutely loyal' to the Communist Party. China is the world's largest jailer of journalists. VPNs are banned though widely used. Social media is heavily censored with platforms like WeChat under Party control.
laws.penalty: Imprisonment for up to life for journalism deemed threatening to national security; journalist licensing required; foreign journalist deportation
exceptions: State media (Xinhua, People's Daily, CGTN) operates as Party mouthpiece

quiz.q: What does China's Central Propaganda Department manage for domestic journalists?
options: The propaganda guidelines that journalists must follow
quiz.explanation: China's Central Propaganda Department (CPD) issues propaganda guidelines that all domestic journalists and media outlets must follow, effectively dictating coverage topics, approved narratives, and forbidden subjects — the operational heart of China's press control system.

laws.title: The Great Firewall — World's Most Comprehensive Internet Censorship
laws.subtitle: China operates the world's most sophisticated internet censorship system with thousands of blocked sites
laws.fullDescription: China's 'Great Firewall' (technically the Golden Shield Project) is the world's most comprehensive internet censorship system. Google, Facebook, Instagram, Twitter/X, YouTube, WhatsApp, Wikipedia, New York Times, BBC, and thousands of other global services are blocked. Chinese platforms (WeChat, Weibo, Douyin/TikTok, Baidu) operate under strict Party guidelines. The Cybersecurity Law (2017) requires platforms to store data in China and assist law enforcement. The Algorithm Regulation (2022) requires AI recommendation systems to follow socialist core values. Real-name registration is required for all online services.
laws.penalty: Internet companies face license revocation and fines; users face criminal penalties for VPN use and prohibited content
exceptions: Special Economic Zones and free trade zones have limited exceptions; VPNs are illegal but widely used

quiz.q: What does China's Algorithm Regulation (2022) require of AI recommendation systems on platforms?
options: Algorithms must follow socialist core values
quiz.explanation: China's 2022 Algorithm Regulation requires AI recommendation systems used by platforms to follow 'socialist core values' — meaning algorithms cannot promote content that challenges Party positions, celebrates individual over collective, or otherwise contradicts official ideology.

laws.title: Digital Yuan (e-CNY) Mandate & Crypto Total Ban
laws.subtitle: China banned all cryptocurrency while aggressively promoting its CBDC
laws.fullDescription: China's People's Bank of China (PBOC) has taken the most aggressive global stance on cryptocurrency: in September 2021, China declared all cryptocurrency transactions illegal, including mining, trading, and providing services. Simultaneously, China has led the world in CBDC deployment — the digital yuan (e-CNY) is issued by PBOC and distributed through state banks, with trials in dozens of cities and millions of users. China's banking sector is dominated by four state-owned megabanks (ICBC, CCB, ABC, BOC). The PBOC implemented strict capital controls limiting individuals to $50,000/year in foreign currency purchases. Financial messaging uses CIPS (Cross-border Interbank Payment System) as an alternative to SWIFT.
laws.penalty: Cryptocurrency trading or mining: criminal charges for organizers, fines for participants; capital control evasion: administrative fines plus asset confiscation; unlicensed financial services: up to 10 years imprisonment
exceptions: Hong Kong maintains separate crypto regulatory framework (separate from mainland China)
CIPS operates alongside (not replacing) SWIFT for international yuan settlements
Free Trade Zones have modified financial regulations

quiz.q: What is China's Central Bank Digital Currency called?
quiz.explanation: China's CBDC is called e-CNY (digital Chinese yuan), also known as the digital yuan or digital RMB. It's issued by the People's Bank of China and distributed through state-owned commercial banks.

laws.title: China Food Safety Law & Strict Post-Scandal Enforcement
laws.subtitle: China overhauled food safety laws after the 2008 melamine milk scandal
laws.fullDescription: China's Food Safety Law (2015, revised 2021) significantly strengthened food safety enforcement following a series of scandals, most notoriously the 2008 melamine-contaminated infant formula crisis that sickened 300,000 babies and killed 6. The State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and NMPA (National Medical Products Administration) jointly enforce food safety. China implemented the strictest infant formula standards in the world post-2008 — every formula batch must be tested and registered. China maintains a 'most severe punishment' approach for food fraud: intentional food safety violations can result in lifetime bans from food industry and life imprisonment. Food delivery platforms (Meituan, Ele.me) must register all restaurants and enforce licensing.
laws.penalty: Intentional food adulteration causing death: life imprisonment or death penalty; food fraud: fines up to 30× illegal income; unlicensed food business: fines up to RMB 100,000; online platform non-compliance: platform can be shut down
exceptions: Traditional home food preparation for personal consumption is unregulated
Agricultural product direct sales by registered farmers have simplified requirements
Pilot free trade zone food imports have expedited safety review processes

quiz.q: What catastrophic food safety scandal in 2008 prompted China's overhaul of its food safety law?
options: Contaminated cooking oil scandal killing hundreds in Guangzhou
Melamine-adulterated infant formula sickening 300,000 babies and killing 6
Fake honey exported to Europe triggering trade sanctions
Mass food poisoning at school canteens across three provinces
quiz.explanation: The 2008 Chinese infant formula scandal, in which melamine (an industrial chemical) was added to dairy products to falsely inflate protein test readings, contaminated baby formula across China. Approximately 300,000 babies were sickened and 6 died. The scandal prompted complete overhaul of China's food safety laws and strictest-in-world infant formula regulations.

laws.title: China Animal Welfare — No Comprehensive National Law
laws.subtitle: China lacks a comprehensive animal welfare law but has sector-specific rules
laws.fullDescription: China does not have a comprehensive national animal welfare law, despite repeated proposals since the 1990s. Animal welfare provisions exist in sector-specific laws — the Wildlife Protection Law (2022), the Animal Epidemic Prevention Law (focusing on disease control), and regulations for experimental animals. China's cultural attitudes toward animals vary enormously — urban pet culture has exploded (300 million+ pets), while rural practices including various animal uses continue with minimal oversight. The traditional medicine industry uses animal products (bear bile, pangolins, rhino horn). Dog meat consumption persists in some regions, including the controversial Yulin Dog Meat Festival. Enforcement of existing wildlife protections is inconsistent.
laws.penalty: Wildlife law violations: fines and criminal penalties; experimental animal regulations: administrative penalties; no specific animal cruelty law penalties
exceptions: Extensive — current framework focuses on disease control and wildlife protection rather than welfare
laws.sourceLabel: 中华人民共和国野生动物保护法 (Wildlife Protection Law 2022)

quiz.q: What is the primary gap in China's animal welfare legal framework?
options: China lacks a comprehensive national animal welfare law — provisions exist only in sector-specific regulations
China bans all companion animals in cities
China's animal welfare laws only apply to foreign-owned animals
quiz.explanation: Despite being the world's largest country by population and a growing pet market of 300+ million animals, China lacks a comprehensive national animal welfare law. Repeated proposals have stalled, leaving animal welfare provisions scattered across sector-specific legislation with significant enforcement gaps.

laws.title: China Civil Code 2021 — Divorce Cooling-Off Period
laws.subtitle: China introduced a 30-day cooling-off period for divorce in 2021
laws.fullDescription: China's family law is part of the comprehensive Civil Code adopted in 2021. China introduced a controversial 30-day 'cooling-off period' for divorces by mutual agreement — either party can withdraw the divorce application within 30 days, then the application is dismissed. This was introduced to reduce 'impulsive divorces' but was criticized by women's rights groups as trapping people in abusive marriages. Same-sex marriage and relationships are not recognized in China. China's default marital property regime is community of acquired property. Divorce rates in China have been rising sharply — the government views divorce as a social problem. China's Civil Code also introduced new provisions on domestic violence and property rights for cohabiting couples.
laws.penalty: Civil enforcement through renmin fayuan (people's courts); support enforcement by court; criminal domestic violence charges under law; contempt orders for custody violations
exceptions: Hunqian caichan xieyi (prenuptial agreement)
Pre-marital property ('hunqian caichan') retained
Judicial divorce available when administrative fails
laws.sourceLabel: 中华人民共和国民法典 (Civil Code 2021) — 婚姻家庭

quiz.q: What controversial divorce provision did China's 2021 Civil Code introduce?
options: China banned divorce for couples with children
A 30-day cooling-off period allowing either party to withdraw a mutual consent divorce application
China made divorce require government approval
China required mandatory 5-year marriage before divorce allowed
quiz.explanation: China's 2021 Civil Code introduced a 30-day 'cooling-off period' for divorces by mutual agreement — during which either spouse can withdraw the divorce application. Criticized by women's rights groups as potentially trapping victims of domestic violence in marriages, the provision reflected the government's concern about rising divorce rates.

laws.title: China Property Law & Land Use Rights
laws.subtitle: State land ownership with 70-year use rights
laws.fullDescription: China's Property Law (Wu Quan Fa, 2007) and Civil Code (2021) govern property rights. All urban land is owned by the state; individuals and corporations can only obtain 'land use rights' (tuyong quanshu) for 40-70 years depending on use type. The 2021 Civil Code automatically extends residential land use rights upon expiration. Rural land is owned collectively by villages; farmers have long-term 'contract rights' for agricultural land (30 years under the Third Plenary Session reforms). The real estate sector's crisis (Evergrande collapse, etc.) from 2021 exposed risks in the pre-sale model. Xi Jinping's 'houses are for living, not speculation' policy directs residential property market regulation.
laws.penalty: Illegal land use: confiscation without compensation; unauthorized construction: demolition and criminal liability
exceptions: Land use rights expire after 40-70 years based on use type
Rural collective land cannot be freely sold to non-members
laws.source: Wu Quan Fa 2007; Minfa Dian 2021; Tudi Guanli Fa
laws.sourceLabel: China Property Law & Land Use Rights

quiz.q: What do Chinese citizens actually own when they 'buy' urban property in China?
options: Land use rights for 40-70 years (not the land itself)
quiz.explanation: In China, all urban land is owned by the state. Buyers receive 'land use rights' for a fixed term (typically 70 years for residential), not freehold ownership of the land itself, though the Civil Code (2021) provides for automatic renewal.

laws.title: China Consumer Rights Protection Law & SAMR
laws.subtitle: E-commerce platform liability and consumer rights
laws.fullDescription: China's Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (1993, revised 2013) provides 7-day return right for online purchases, and the 2019 E-Commerce Law holds platforms jointly liable for sales by third-party merchants if they fail to act on consumer complaints. The State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) enforces consumer law with powerful administrative tools. The 7-day no-reason return policy for e-commerce has been significant for Taobao, JD.com, and Pinduoduo users. The 'Double 11' (November 11 shopping festival) has generated consumer complaints about fake discounts. China's 'san bao' (three guarantees) warranty system requires repair, replacement, or refund.
laws.penalty: E-Commerce Law platform liability: fine up to RMB 2 million; product defects: 'san bao' three guarantees apply
exceptions: E-Commerce Law 2019: platforms liable for third-party merchant consumer harm
7-day no-reason return right for online purchases
laws.source: Consumer Rights Protection Law 1993; E-Commerce Law 2019

quiz.q: What major liability rule does China's 2019 E-Commerce Law impose on platforms like Taobao?
options: Platforms are never liable for third-party sellers
Platforms are jointly liable with third-party merchants if they fail to act on consumer complaints
Foreign platforms are exempt from liability
quiz.explanation: China's E-Commerce Law (2019) holds e-commerce platforms jointly liable with third-party merchants when platforms fail to take action on consumer complaints about those merchants — a strong incentive for platforms like Taobao and JD.com to self-regulate their merchant ecosystem.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国宪法 — Constitution of the PRC
laws.subtitle: The legal foundation of the Chinese Communist Party's rule
laws.fullDescription: China's Constitution (1982, amended 2018) establishes the People's Republic as a 'socialist state under the people's democratic dictatorship led by the working class and based on the worker-peasant alliance'. The Chinese Communist Party's leading role is enshrined in the preamble. The 2018 amendment removed presidential term limits (allowing Xi Jinping to serve indefinitely), added 'Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era', and strengthened anti-corruption provisions. The National People's Congress (全国人民代表大会) formally enacts laws, though the CCP's Politburo Standing Committee holds actual governing power.
laws.penalty: Challenging CCP leadership: prosecuted as subversion of state power under Criminal Law Article 105, up to life imprisonment. Speech deemed to 'split the nation': up to life.
exceptions: Special Administrative Regions of Hong Kong and Macau operate under 'one country, two systems' with separate legal frameworks
Tibet and Xinjiang Autonomous Regions have nominal autonomy
National security exceptions broad under National Security Law
laws.sourceLabel: 全国人民代表大会 — National People's Congress

quiz.q: What significant change did China's 2018 constitutional amendment make?
options: It established an independent Supreme Court with judicial review
It removed presidential term limits, enabling Xi Jinping to serve indefinitely
It granted Hong Kong permanent autonomy status
It established a second legislative chamber
quiz.explanation: China's 2018 constitutional amendment removed the two-term presidential limit that had been in place since 1982 — designed to prevent another Mao-style lifetime rule. The removal allows Xi Jinping to serve as president indefinitely, representing a significant centralization of power.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国刑法 — Criminal Law of the PRC
laws.subtitle: China's criminal code with broad political offense provisions
laws.fullDescription: China's Criminal Law (1979, extensively revised) covers conventional crimes plus uniquely broad political offenses. Key provisions include 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble' (寻衅滋事) — used to prosecute social media posts, protests, and petitioners — and 'subversion of state power' used against lawyers, journalists, and activists. The criminal process emphasizes 'leniency for those who confess', creating strong pressure to plead guilty. China retains capital punishment for 46 offenses including non-violent crimes like drug trafficking and certain economic crimes. China is estimated to execute more people than the rest of the world combined (thousands annually, figures classified).
laws.penalty: Drug trafficking over 50g heroin: mandatory death penalty. Corruption over ¥3M: death penalty or life. Subversion of state power: up to life imprisonment.
exceptions: Death sentences for most crimes (except intentional homicide, rape of minor, terrorism) receive 2-year suspension, often commuted to life if 'good behavior'
Mental incapacity recognized as defense
Juveniles under 14 not criminally liable; 14-18 reduced penalties
laws.sourceLabel: 全国人民代表大会 — National People's Congress

quiz.q: What crime does China uniquely prosecute under 'picking quarrels and provoking trouble'?
options: Broadly used against social media posts, protests, and petitioners critical of authorities
quiz.explanation: 'Picking quarrels and provoking trouble' (寻衅滋事) is a vague catch-all offense used extremely broadly — to prosecute critical social media posts, protesters, citizens who petition for redress of grievances, lawyers representing sensitive cases, and journalists. Its vagueness makes it a flexible tool for suppressing dissent.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国网络安全法 — Cybersecurity Law
laws.subtitle: China's data localization and internet control framework
laws.fullDescription: China's Cybersecurity Law (2017) requires 'critical information infrastructure' operators to store data in China, undergo security assessments before transferring data abroad, and use 'secure and controllable' products. Combined with the Data Security Law (2021) and Personal Information Protection Law (2021), China has built a comprehensive digital governance framework. The Great Firewall (防火长城) blocks thousands of foreign websites including Google, Facebook, YouTube, and WhatsApp. VPN use is restricted — permitted for businesses but individual use is illegal. Data portability to foreign governments faces additional restrictions under the 2021 Data Security Law.
laws.penalty: Failure to store data in China: up to ¥1M fine and service suspension. Providing data to foreign authorities without Chinese approval: up to ¥10M fine.
exceptions: Free Trade Zone operators may have modified data transfer rules
Academic and scientific data sharing may receive exemptions
Approved cross-border data transfers permitted after security assessment
laws.sourceLabel: 国家互联网信息办公室 — Cyberspace Administration of China

quiz.q: What does China's 'Great Firewall' (防火长城) block?
options: Thousands of foreign platforms including Google, Facebook, YouTube, and WhatsApp
Only explicitly pornographic or violent content
Websites hosted outside of approved CDN providers
quiz.explanation: China's Great Firewall blocks thousands of foreign websites — most prominently Google (all services), Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, Twitter/X, WhatsApp, and countless news sites. Chinese users access domestic equivalents (Baidu, WeChat, Weibo, Youku) or use VPNs — which individuals are technically prohibited from using.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国外资法 — Foreign Investment Law
laws.subtitle: Rules governing foreign companies operating in China
laws.fullDescription: China's Foreign Investment Law (2020) replaced three earlier laws governing foreign-invested enterprises. It establishes national treatment for foreign investors (equal treatment to domestic companies) in non-restricted sectors, but maintains the Negative List — sectors where foreign investment is prohibited or restricted. China's Negative List has been progressively shortened. Foreign investment in media, internet services, education, and healthcare faces restrictions. Variable Interest Entity (VIE) structures allow foreign investors to effectively control Chinese companies in restricted sectors through contractual arrangements — legally gray but tolerated for major tech companies.
laws.penalty: Operating in prohibited sectors: forced divestiture and fines. Failure to file FDI registration: administrative penalties.
exceptions: Free Trade Zones (Shanghai, Shenzhen, etc.) have shorter negative lists
Strategic industries benefit from investment incentives
Certain sectors opened to qualified foreign limited partnerships
laws.sourceLabel: 商务部 — Ministry of Commerce China

quiz.q: What is the 'VIE structure' commonly used by China-based companies listed abroad?
options: A type of Chinese limited partnership popular with foreign investors
A contractual structure allowing foreign investors to control Chinese companies in restricted sectors
A government-issued special license for foreign-owned banks
A joint venture model requiring 50-50 Chinese-foreign ownership
quiz.explanation: Variable Interest Entity (VIE) structures use contractual arrangements to give foreign investors effective economic control over Chinese entities in sectors restricted to foreign direct ownership. Chinese tech giants (Alibaba, Baidu, Tencent) used VIEs to list overseas. The structure exists in legal gray area — technically unauthorized but tolerated — creating regulatory risk for investors.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国国家安全法 — National Security Law (Hong Kong)
laws.subtitle: Beijing's security law imposing mainland jurisdiction over Hong Kong
laws.fullDescription: The National Security Law for Hong Kong (2020) was enacted by Beijing's National People's Congress Standing Committee, bypassing Hong Kong's own legislature, following the 2019 protests. It criminalizes secession, subversion, terrorism, and collusion with foreign forces — with maximum sentences of life imprisonment. The law applies globally: foreign nationals who have never visited Hong Kong can be charged. It established a mainland security agency in Hong Kong with powers over certain cases. Over 100 pro-democracy figures have been prosecuted, including newspaper owner Jimmy Lai. The NSL effectively dismantled Hong Kong's opposition political movement.
laws.penalty: Secession, subversion, terrorism, foreign collusion: 10 years to life imprisonment. Incitement offenses: up to 5 years.
exceptions: Cases involving 'complex foreign elements' may be tried on mainland China under mainland law
PRC security agents operating in Hong Kong immune from local prosecution
Mainland courts have jurisdiction when mainland security agency takes charge

quiz.q: What made Hong Kong's 2020 National Security Law unusual in how it was enacted?
options: It was passed by overwhelming 98% vote in Hong Kong's legislature
Beijing enacted it directly, bypassing Hong Kong's own legislature
It was imposed by international treaty
It was adopted by public referendum in Hong Kong
quiz.explanation: Beijing enacted the National Security Law by invoking the National People's Congress Standing Committee's power under Annex III of the Basic Law — meaning it was imposed directly without going through Hong Kong's own Legislative Council. Critics said this violated the 'one country, two systems' framework and Hong Kong's constitutional autonomy.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国劳动合同法 — Labor Contract Law
laws.subtitle: China's employment contract requirements and worker rights
laws.fullDescription: China's Labor Contract Law (2008) requires written employment contracts, limits probationary periods (maximum 6 months for contracts over 3 years), and requires severance for involuntary termination. Open-ended contracts must be offered after two consecutive fixed-term contracts or 10 years of employment. The law significantly strengthened worker rights on paper. Implementation varies enormously: the '996' work culture (9am-9pm, 6 days) is widespread in tech, though courts have ruled it illegal. Labor disputes are adjudicated through a mandatory arbitration-first process. China's manufacturing sector relies heavily on internal migrants (农民工, migrant workers) with complex residency (户口) implications.
laws.penalty: Failure to sign written contract: double wages for each month without contract. Wrongful termination: 2x severance. Child labor: ¥5,000-50,000 fine per child.
exceptions: Fixed-term contracts may replace open-ended under specific conditions
Probationary periods reduce for shorter contract durations
Part-time employees (under 4 hours/day) have simplified contract requirements
laws.sourceLabel: 人力资源和社会保障部 — Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security

quiz.q: What is China's controversial '996' work culture, and what did courts say about it?
options: Working 9 hours on Saturday for 6 months, which courts upheld
Working 9am-9pm, 6 days per week in tech companies — courts ruled this practice illegal
Working with 9-minute breaks every 6 hours, legalized in 2019
A term for 9 annual holidays over 6 months
quiz.explanation: '996' (9am to 9pm, 6 days per week) describes the overwork culture prevalent in Chinese tech companies like Alibaba and JD.com. In 2021, Chinese courts ruled that mandatory 996 schedules violate labor law — though enforcement in practice is weak and cultural pressure to overwork remains intense.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国大气污染防治法 — Air Pollution Prevention Law
laws.subtitle: China's response to severe urban air pollution
laws.fullDescription: China's Air Pollution Prevention and Control Law (2015, revised 2018) responds to the severe air pollution crisis epitomized by Beijing's 'airpocalypse' events (PM2.5 readings exceeding 900 μg/m³ vs WHO safe limit of 15). The law requires 'joint prevention' across regional boundaries, sets emission standards for vehicles and industry, and restricts coal burning in key areas. China's 'War on Pollution' (2014-2020) achieved significant improvements: Beijing's annual PM2.5 fell from 89.5 μg/m³ (2013) to 33 μg/m³ (2022). China is simultaneously the world's largest CO2 emitter and solar/wind power installer.
laws.penalty: Exceeding emission standards: fines up to ¥1M/day (continuing violations multiply daily). Operating without permit: immediate shutdown. Environmental crimes: up to 7 years imprisonment.
exceptions: Agricultural burning exemptions apply in rural areas during specific seasons
Strategic industries may receive emission waivers during economic downturns
Emergency productions for national security have modified standards
laws.sourceLabel: 生态环境部 — Ministry of Ecology and Environment

quiz.q: What dramatic air quality improvement did Beijing achieve from 2013 to 2022?
options: PM2.5 increased 20% as pollution worsened with industrialization
PM2.5 annual average fell from 89.5 to 33 μg/m³ through aggressive anti-pollution measures
Beijing achieved WHO clean air standards by 2020
No measurable improvement — the data is disputed
quiz.explanation: Beijing's annual PM2.5 concentration fell from 89.5 μg/m³ in 2013 (after a notorious 'airpocalypse') to 33 μg/m³ in 2022 — still above WHO guidelines but a roughly 63% improvement in under a decade. This resulted from banning coal heating in urban areas, relocating steel plants, and restricting vehicles — demonstrating that China's 'War on Pollution' produced measurable results.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国物权法 — Property Rights Law
laws.subtitle: China's unique land ownership and property rights framework
laws.fullDescription: China's Property Rights Law (2007, superseded by Civil Code 2021) establishes a system where all land is owned by the state (urban) or rural collectives — individuals may only hold land use rights (土地使用权, typically 70 years for residential). This land ownership structure enables mass demolitions for development: the government can reclaim land use rights with compensation, leading to famous confrontations with nail house owners (钉子户) who refuse to leave. Forced demolitions (强拆) have been a major source of social conflict. Urban residents' 70-year land use rights expiration has become a major policy concern.
laws.penalty: Illegal construction on collective land: demolition orders and fines. Unauthorized transfer of land use rights: contract void and profits forfeited.
exceptions: Special Economic Zones may have modified land tenure rules
Foreign-invested enterprises may hold land use rights for project duration
Rural land may be 'circulated' but not sold to non-farmers
laws.sourceLabel: 全国人民代表大会 — National People's Congress

quiz.q: What is a 'nail house' (钉子户) in Chinese property law?
options: A property with illegal additions that violate building codes
A homeowner who refuses to vacate when their land is reclaimed for development, often holding out for better compensation
A property encumbered by multiple competing mortgages
A building designated as historical that cannot be demolished
quiz.explanation: Nail houses (钉子户) are properties where owners refuse to vacate when the government reclaims land use rights for development. Photos of lone houses surrounded by construction sites became iconic symbols of tensions between China's development drive and property rights. Some owners hold out for years, achieving much better compensation — but others face forced demolition.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国银行业监督管理法 — Banking Supervision Law
laws.subtitle: China's banking regulatory framework and state-owned bank dominance
laws.fullDescription: China's banking sector is dominated by five state-owned commercial banks: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), China Construction Bank, Agricultural Bank of China, Bank of China, and Bank of Communications — collectively managing assets exceeding $20 trillion. The National Financial Regulatory Administration (NFRA, established 2023, replacing CBIRC) oversees banking. China's shadow banking sector has been a major regulatory concern, particularly Ant Group's Alipay lending products. The 2020-2023 regulatory crackdown on fintech followed Jack Ma's speech criticizing regulators. State-directed credit to policy priorities remains a distinctive feature.
laws.penalty: Operating unlicensed banking services: up to ¥5M fine and criminal prosecution. Major financial fraud: up to life imprisonment and property confiscation.
exceptions: Policy banks (CDB, EXIM, Agricultural Development Bank) operate under separate mandate
Rural credit cooperatives have modified capital requirements
Financial institutions in Free Trade Zones have expanded operational permissions
laws.sourceLabel: 国家金融监督管理总局 — National Financial Regulatory Administration

quiz.q: What event triggered China's major 2020-2023 regulatory crackdown on fintech companies?
options: A major banking collapse threatening the financial system
Jack Ma's speech criticizing Chinese financial regulators, followed by suspension of Ant Group's IPO
Foreign regulators threatening to delist Chinese tech companies
A hacking incident exposing financial data of millions of users
quiz.explanation: Jack Ma's October 2020 speech comparing Chinese banks to 'pawnshops' and criticizing regulators preceded the sudden suspension of Ant Group's planned $37 billion IPO (would have been the world's largest). This marked the start of a broader tech regulatory crackdown that wiped hundreds of billions from Chinese tech valuations and put Ma out of public view for months.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国基本医疗卫生与健康促进法 — Basic Healthcare Law
laws.subtitle: China's healthcare system and universal coverage expansion
laws.fullDescription: China's Basic Medical and Health Care Promotion Law (2020) establishes the framework for China's healthcare system. China has expanded insurance coverage dramatically: Basic Medical Insurance now covers 1.3+ billion people. The system includes Urban Employee Basic Medical Insurance (城镇职工医疗保险) and Urban-Rural Residents Insurance (城乡居民医疗保险). Despite broad coverage, out-of-pocket costs remain high (30%+) and quality varies dramatically between urban hospitals and rural clinics. China's COVID-19 response — 'dynamic zero COVID' maintained until December 2022 — demonstrated both the capacity for extreme public health measures and eventual limits of lockdown strategies.
laws.penalty: Healthcare fraud under insurance system: criminal prosecution. Illegal medical practice: license revocation and up to 3 years imprisonment.
exceptions: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) practitioners have separate licensing track
Charitable medical services in underserved areas may receive operational flexibility
Emergency treatment must be provided regardless of insurance status
laws.sourceLabel: 国家卫生健康委员会 — National Health Commission

quiz.q: How many people does China's Basic Medical Insurance system cover?
options: Only urban formal workers — approximately 300 million
About 700 million people in major cities
1.3+ billion people through multiple insurance programs
Coverage is voluntary — approximately 500 million enrolled
quiz.explanation: China has achieved remarkable coverage breadth: Basic Medical Insurance covers over 1.3 billion people through a combination of Urban Employee Medical Insurance (for formal workers) and Urban-Rural Residents Insurance (for others). However, coverage depth — the actual percentage of costs covered — varies significantly, with out-of-pocket costs remaining high at 30%+.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国出入境管理法 — Exit-Entry Administration Law
laws.subtitle: China's travel restrictions and exit ban system
laws.fullDescription: China's Exit-Entry Administration Law (2012) regulates movement of citizens and foreigners. China maintains a system of exit bans (边控) that prevent individuals from leaving the country — used for corruption investigations, civil litigation, business disputes, and national security. Exit bans can be imposed without criminal charges and often without notification. Foreign nationals have been detained in China as leverage in diplomatic or commercial disputes (so-called 'hostage diplomacy' allegations). The Social Credit System intersects with travel restrictions — individuals with low scores may be banned from buying airline or high-speed rail tickets.
laws.penalty: Illegal border crossing: up to 1 year detention or up to 7 years for organized people smuggling. Assisting illegal exit: up to 7 years.
exceptions: Residents of Hong Kong and Macau travel to mainland under separate permit (回乡证)
Taiwan residents use 'Taiwan Compatriot Permit'
APEC Business Travel Card holders have expedited immigration in participating economies
laws.sourceLabel: 公安部 — Ministry of Public Security

quiz.q: What is China's 'exit ban' (边控) system?
options: A requirement for all citizens to carry passports when traveling domestically
Restricting individuals from leaving China — imposed for investigations, disputes, or security — often without prior notice
A customs inspection regime for exports
Requiring visa applications for exit rather than entry
quiz.explanation: China's exit ban system (边控) allows authorities to prevent individuals from leaving the country for reasons ranging from criminal investigation to civil disputes to national security. Bans can be imposed without criminal charges, sometimes without notification, and have been applied to foreign nationals — leading to allegations of 'hostage diplomacy' where foreigners are held as diplomatic leverage.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国义务教育法 — Compulsory Education Law
laws.subtitle: Nine years of mandatory education and the Gaokao university entrance exam
laws.fullDescription: China's Compulsory Education Law mandates 9 years of schooling (6 years primary + 3 years junior secondary) for all children. The '双减' (double reduction) policy (2021) dramatically restricted after-school tutoring companies — wiping out a $100+ billion industry — to reduce 'educational involution' (内卷) and pressure on students. The Gaokao (高考, National College Entrance Examination) is China's single most important exam, lasting 9 hours over 2-3 days, with scores determining university admission. It is considered one of the world's most high-stakes exams, with 13+ million students sitting annually. Cheating in Gaokao carries criminal penalties.
laws.penalty: Gaokao cheating: criminal prosecution up to 7 years imprisonment under Anti-Cheating Law (2015). Illegal tutoring operations: fines and business closure.
exceptions: Ethnic minority students receive bonus points (加分) on Gaokao
Children of military personnel may take exam in different provinces
Students with disabilities receive extended time and accommodation
laws.sourceLabel: 教育部 — Ministry of Education China

quiz.q: What did China's 2021 'double reduction' (双减) policy do to the tutoring industry?
options: Doubled the number of allowed tutoring hours per week
Dramatically restricted after-school tutoring companies, wiping out a $100B+ industry
Reduced tutoring costs by 50% through price controls
Made tutoring mandatory for all students in core subjects
quiz.explanation: China's 2021 '双减' policy prohibited after-school tutoring companies from teaching core academic subjects on weekends, holidays, and school vacations. This effectively destroyed a $100+ billion industry almost overnight — companies like New Oriental and TAL saw stock prices collapse 90%+. The policy aimed to reduce educational pressure but displaced thousands of workers.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国土地管理法 — Land Administration Law
laws.subtitle: Regulating China's land use, rural land rights, and government acquisition
laws.fullDescription: China's Land Administration Law (1986, revised 2019) governs land use and government acquisition. All urban land is state-owned; rural land is collectively owned. Local governments sell land use rights as a primary revenue source — land finance (土地财政) made up 30-40% of local government revenue at peak. China's property boom was fueled by this system. The 2019 revision allowed rural collectively-owned construction land to enter the market directly (previously only possible through government acquisition), potentially transforming rural land economics. Land acquisition for public purposes requires compensation, but disputes over adequacy are common.
laws.penalty: Illegal occupation of agricultural land: 1 to 10 years imprisonment for severe cases. Unauthorized conversion of farmland to construction: heavy fines and demolition.
exceptions: State projects designated as 'national key construction projects' have simplified acquisition procedures
Rural residents retain house-site use rights (宅基地) for life
Economic development zones have modified land classification rules
laws.sourceLabel: 自然资源部 — Ministry of Natural Resources

quiz.q: What unique role does land play in China's local government finance?
options: Land is taxed at 5% of value annually to fund local services
Land use right sales generated 30-40% of local government revenue at peak
All land revenue goes to central government
Local governments own no land — they are landlords of the state
quiz.explanation: China's 'land finance' (土地财政) system emerged because local governments receive little tax revenue but bear major expenditure responsibilities. They compensated by acquiring rural land and selling urban land use rights to developers at large profits. At peak, land sales represented 30-40% of local government revenue — creating strong incentives to develop land and fueling the property boom.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国禁毒法 — Drug Control Law
laws.subtitle: China's strict prohibition on narcotics with harsh penalties
laws.fullDescription: China's Drug Control Law (2008) and Criminal Law establish severe penalties for drug offenses. Trafficking 50+ grams of heroin or methamphetamine is punishable by death. China is one of the world's largest executors for drug offenses. Drug rehabilitation is distinctive: China operates Compulsory Drug Treatment (强制戒毒) — administrative detention (not criminal prosecution) for drug users for 2-3 years in government facilities. Xi Jinping has declared a 'people's war on drugs'. Fentanyl precursor chemicals from China have been a source of diplomatic tension with the US, with China adding them to controlled substances lists in 2019.
laws.penalty: Trafficking 50g+ heroin: death penalty. Manufacturing or trafficking 1kg+ methamphetamine: death. Possession for personal use: administrative detention 10-15 days or compulsory rehabilitation.
exceptions: Medical use of controlled substances with prescription is permitted
Research institutions licensed for controlled substance studies
Methadone maintenance therapy legally authorized at approved clinics
laws.sourceLabel: 中国禁毒 — National Narcotics Control Commission

quiz.q: What is distinctive about how China handles drug users compared to traffickers?
options: Drug users receive death penalty; traffickers receive 10 years
Drug users are typically sent to administrative compulsory rehabilitation centers, not criminal prosecution
There is no distinction — all drug offenses receive the same penalty
Drug users receive suspended sentences on first offense
quiz.explanation: China's system distinguishes between trafficking (criminal prosecution with potential death penalty) and drug use (administrative detention). Users typically face Compulsory Drug Treatment (强制戒毒) — 2-3 year administrative detention in rehabilitation facilities — without going through criminal court. This can be imposed repeatedly for relapse.

laws.title: 互联网信息服务管理办法 — Internet Information Services Measures
laws.subtitle: China's regulatory framework for online content and platforms
laws.fullDescription: China's Internet Information Services Measures and related regulations create a comprehensive framework for controlling online content. Platform operators must obtain Internet Content Provider (ICP) licenses. Content rules prohibit anything 'endangering national security', 'damaging national unity', or 'disrupting social order' — broadly interpreted. Algorithms must be registered with the Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC). Real-name registration (实名制) requires all online users to register with their actual identity. Social media platforms are legally liable for user content and face massive fines for failing to remove prohibited content quickly. WeChat, Weibo, and Douyin (TikTok's Chinese version) implement extensive content moderation.
laws.penalty: Operating without ICP license: fines and service shutdown. Failing to remove prohibited content: fines up to ¥3M and service suspension.
exceptions: Academic and research institutions have modified content access permissions
Government-approved VPNs permitted for business use
Foreign news organizations may establish bureaus under press accreditation
laws.sourceLabel: 国家互联网信息办公室 — Cyberspace Administration of China

quiz.q: What is China's real-name registration (实名制) requirement?
options: Physical ID required to purchase internet-connected devices
All online users must register with actual identity verified against national ID database
Online opinions must be signed with real name when published
Internet cafes require registration of all users
quiz.explanation: China's real-name registration system requires users to verify their actual identity (national ID number) when registering for online services — social media, messaging apps, online games, and more. This links online activities to real identities, enabling identification of users who post prohibited content and serving as a significant deterrent to anonymous dissent.

laws.title: 人口与计划生育法 — Population and Family Planning Law
laws.subtitle: From one-child to three-child policy: China's demographic experiments
laws.fullDescription: China's one-child policy (1980-2015) was the most sweeping population control experiment in history, applied to ~36% of the population (exceptions for rural areas, ethnic minorities, and parents who were both only children). It prevented an estimated 200-400 million births but created severe demographic imbalances: aging population, gender imbalance from sex-selective abortion (106:100 male:female birth ratio), and a shrinking workforce. The policy was relaxed to two children in 2015 and three in 2021. In 2023, China officially entered population decline — the first time since 1961. The government now offers financial incentives to have more children.
laws.penalty: Exceeding birth limits historically: heavy fines ('social maintenance fees', 社会抚养费) of 3-10x annual income, loss of government job, forced sterilization in some cases.
exceptions: Rural families where first child was a girl often permitted second child
Ethnic minorities in certain regions permitted more children
Parents who were themselves only children permitted two children under reforms
laws.sourceLabel: 国家卫生健康委员会 — National Health Commission

quiz.q: What demographic consequence of China's one-child policy is now driving policy reversal?
options: Population became too urbanized to support agriculture
Aging population and declining workforce creating economic pressure, with China entering population decline in 2023
quiz.explanation: China's one-child policy created a demographic time bomb: a rapidly aging population with fewer working-age adults to support them, and declining birth rates. In 2023, China's total population shrank for the first time since 1961 — prompting policy reversal to encourage more births with financial incentives, though cultural and economic factors have made reversing low birth rates difficult.

laws.title: 长江保护法 — Yangtze River Protection Law
laws.subtitle: Protecting China's most important river ecosystem
laws.fullDescription: China's Yangtze River Protection Law (2021) establishes comprehensive protections for the 6,300km river basin housing 400+ million people. The law imposes a 10-year fishing moratorium (2021-2030) in the main channel and tributary lakes, addressing severe depletion of fish stocks. Industrial development in the 1km riparian zone is restricted. Chemical plants along the Yangtze must be relocated. The Three Gorges Dam (三峡大坝) — the world's largest hydroelectric project — displaced 1.3 million people and has dramatically altered the river ecosystem. The Yangtze River dolphin (白鱀豚) was declared functionally extinct in 2006; the Yangtze finless porpoise is critically endangered.
laws.penalty: Illegal fishing in protected zones: criminal prosecution under fisheries law, equipment confiscation. Industrial violations: up to ¥5M fine.
exceptions: Traditional fishing communities receive transition support and limited licensed access
Scientific research on fish populations permitted under license
Cultural and ceremonial fishing by ethnic minorities may receive exemptions
laws.sourceLabel: 水利部 — Ministry of Water Resources

quiz.q: What dramatic conservation measure does China's Yangtze River Protection Law impose?
options: Complete prohibition on all human activity within 5km of the river
A 10-year total fishing moratorium in the main channel to allow fish stock recovery
Mandatory relocation of all cities within 100km of the river
Banning hydroelectric development on all tributaries
quiz.explanation: China imposed a 10-year total commercial and recreational fishing moratorium (2021-2030) in the Yangtze River main channel and major connected lakes. This radical measure responds to fish stocks declining to near-collapse levels from overfishing, pollution, and dam construction. Hundreds of thousands of fishermen received compensation and job retraining.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国监察法 — Supervision Law
laws.subtitle: Xi Jinping's anti-corruption framework and the National Supervisory Commission
laws.fullDescription: China's Supervision Law (2018) established the National Supervisory Commission (NSC) — a new state organ parallel to the Supreme People's Court — to investigate corruption by all public officials. The NSC merged the CCP's Central Commission for Discipline Inspection (CCDI) with government anti-corruption bodies. The NSC uses 'Liuzhi' (留置, formerly 'Shuanggui') — a form of detention outside the criminal justice system where officials can be held for up to 6 months without charge, without access to lawyers, and without court oversight. Since 2012, Xi's anti-corruption campaign has investigated 4+ million officials.
laws.penalty: Corruption: up to death penalty for amounts over ¥3 million. Officials accepting bribes: up to life imprisonment. All illicit gains plus fines confiscated.
exceptions: Officials who voluntarily report corruption and cooperate receive leniency — 'leniency for confession' principle
Lesser officials receive administrative sanctions (demerit, demotion) for minor violations
First-time offenses with restitution of proceeds may receive suspended sentences
laws.sourceLabel: 中央纪律检查委员会 — Central Commission for Discipline Inspection

quiz.q: What is 'Liuzhi' (留置) detention used in China's anti-corruption investigations?
options: A form of house arrest with electronic monitoring ankle bracelet
Detention outside the normal criminal justice system, without lawyers or court oversight, for up to 6 months
A special fast-track criminal prosecution for corruption cases
Voluntary cooperation program where officials surrender ill-gotten gains
quiz.explanation: Liuzhi detention allows the National Supervisory Commission to hold officials for up to 6 months without access to lawyers, without court oversight, and outside the normal criminal justice system. Critics including legal scholars and bar associations have raised due process concerns. Supporters say it is necessary to investigate officials who might otherwise destroy evidence or flee.

laws.title: 中国制造2025 — Made in China 2025 Policy Framework
laws.subtitle: China's industrial policy for technological self-reliance
laws.fullDescription: Made in China 2025 (中国制造2025, 2015) is China's strategic plan to move from low-cost manufacturing to dominating 10 advanced technology sectors: semiconductors, aerospace, AI, electric vehicles, robotics, biopharma, new materials, rail, maritime, and agricultural machinery. Domestic market share targets: 70% by 2025 in key sectors. State subsidies, technology transfer requirements, and government procurement preferences support the plan. The plan became a major flashpoint in the US-China trade war — Trump administration tariffs explicitly targeted MIC2025 sectors. In response, China stopped publicly promoting the plan while continuing its substance under different names.
laws.penalty: Violations of industrial policy incentive terms: repayment of subsidies with interest. State enterprises misusing national champion support: administrative sanctions.
exceptions: Foreign companies partnering on technology transfer may receive investment approvals in restricted sectors
Companies meeting domestic content requirements receive preferential procurement
National security exemptions apply to all sensitive technology sectors
laws.sourceLabel: 工业和信息化部 — Ministry of Industry and Information Technology

quiz.q: Why did China stop publicly promoting 'Made in China 2025' after 2018?
options: The plan was completed ahead of schedule
US-China trade war made the plan a diplomatic liability — China continued the substance under different names
The plan was abandoned in favor of 'Dual Circulation' strategy
WTO ruled it violated international trade agreements
quiz.explanation: China stopped publicly referencing 'Made in China 2025' after it became a central US trade war grievance — Trump cited it as evidence of China's unfair industrial policy. However, the actual programs, subsidies, and targets continued under different terminology. The rebranding was diplomatic optics rather than a substantive policy change.

laws.title: 中华人民共和国对外关系法 — Foreign Relations Law
laws.subtitle: China's legal framework for asserting countermeasures and jurisdictional reach
laws.fullDescription: China's Foreign Relations Law (2023) codifies Beijing's authority to impose countermeasures against foreign states, organizations, and individuals acting against China's interests. It requires all individuals and organizations in China to support Chinese foreign policy objectives. The law provides the legal basis for retaliating against foreign sanctions (like those imposed by the US, EU, and UK over Xinjiang and Hong Kong). China has implemented 'anti-foreign sanctions law' (反外国制裁法, 2021) allowing Chinese courts to order compensation from foreign individuals and entities that implement foreign sanctions. This creates legal conflict for multinational corporations subject to both regimes.
laws.penalty: Compliance with foreign sanctions that China opposes: civil liability in Chinese courts, business license revocation. Failure to support Chinese diplomatic positions: unclear but potentially severe.
exceptions: Diplomatic missions have immunity under Vienna Convention
UN-authorized multilateral sanctions may be treated differently from unilateral sanctions
Academic and cultural exchanges generally exempt from Foreign Relations Law application
laws.sourceLabel: 全国人民代表大会 — National People's Congress

quiz.q: What dilemma does China's Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law (2021) create for multinational companies?
options: They must choose which country to register in
Companies may face legal liability in China for complying with US/EU sanctions, and liability abroad for not complying — creating impossible conflict
They must submit all business plans to both Chinese and foreign regulators
They are prohibited from operating in both China and sanctioned countries simultaneously
quiz.explanation: China's Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law creates an impossible conflict for multinationals: complying with US or EU sanctions against China-linked entities (required by US/EU law, with criminal penalties for violation) potentially makes them liable in Chinese courts. Not complying risks US/EU penalties. Navigating this 'legal conflict of laws' has become a major compliance challenge for global businesses.
